messages:
rachel: Hey, hitting flaky behavior on the Kotlin client when streaming large responses. Looks like OkHttp sometimes drops the stream and our retry interceptor replays the request which causes duplicate partial data. Anyone seen this?

mike: Yep, retries on streaming requests are sketchy. OkHttp's automatic retry/connection-failure logic can close the underlying stream and you can't re-stream the same body. Did you use retryOnConnectionFailure(true)?

rachel: We have a custom RetryInterceptor that retries on 5xx. Client is built with: 
```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(true) // default-ish
  .addInterceptor(RetryInterceptor())
  .build()
```
The streaming endpoint uses request bodyless GET but response is long-lived (server-sent events-ish).

emily: For long-lived responses you should disable retryOnConnectionFailure and avoid replaying streaming requests. OkHttp can automatically reconnect, but not rehydrate a streaming response. Suggest constructing a separate client for streaming endpoints: no retries, short timeouts where appropriate.

juan: Also, if you're using an interceptor that reads the response body to determine retryable errors, that will consume the stream. Make sure the interceptor only checks headers/status and doesn't buffer the whole body.

rachel: Good call. Our retry interceptor reads response.body?.string() to inspect error details. Oops.

mike: That explains it. .string() consumes the body. For non-idempotent streams wrap error parsing with response.peekBody(limit) or only check status. For streaming you can use: 
```kotlin
val peek = response.peekBody(1024) // safe small peek
// parse peek for error meta, then decide
```
But avoid retrying after you've consumed any part of the actual stream.

emily: Quick checklist:
• Use client with retryOnConnectionFailure(false) for streaming
• Make sure interceptors don't .string() the full body
• Use Call.clone() for safe retries only when request body is repeatable

rachel: Thanks. Separate but related: I'm also seeing ClassCastExceptions in apps embedding our SDK when using Gson vs Jackson — eg com/google/gson/JsonObject can't be cast to com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode. Suspect shading issues across downstream projects.

juan: That's usually multiple JSON libs on the classpath with different versions or relocations. If the SDK ships a bundled gson/jackson that isn't relocated, apps that also include gson/jackson can end up with duplicate classes and weird casts.

mike: We intentionally shaded some deps previously but maybe missed the JSON modules. For Gradle Shadow plugin use relocation: 
```groovy
shadowJar {
  relocate 'com.google.gson', 'com.redwood.shaded.com.google.gson'
  relocate 'com.fasterxml.jackson', 'com.redwood.shaded.com.fasterxml.jackson'
  relocate 'org.slf4j', 'com.redwood.shaded.org.slf4j'
}
```
That ensures the SDK's versions don't conflict with host apps.

emily: Another option: prefer one JSON lib as the SDK surface (e.g., only expose jackson on public API) and make the other implementation internal and shaded. That reduces casting issues for consumers.

rachel: We're currently exposing both (user can pass either) which complicates things. If we shade both it's safer but increases jar size. Concerned about downstream apps that use custom ObjectMappers.

juan: If you accept ObjectMapper/Gson instance from the host (in config) and don't bundle the public classes you can avoid shading those API types. I.e., don't ship com.fasterxml.jackson classes in the SDK's public package — take them as provided or document the required version. But that's tougher for self-contained builds.

mike: Pragmatic path: 1) Shade internal-only JSON modules to avoid conflicts; 2) Keep public model POJOs in our package and provide adapters so hosts can plug in their own mappers; 3) Add contract tests.

emily: Also add a note in the README about shading/relocations and the recommended Gradle/Maven rules for consumers. A short migration blurb helps.

rachel: I'll open a PR to: (a) create a dedicated OkHttp client for streaming endpoints (no retries, no body-consuming interceptors), (b) add shadow relocation for gson/jackson internal modules, (c) update README with guidance. PR draft: #3421.

build-bot: Deploy check passed for branch rachel/streaming-fix (unit tests + integration smoke). :white_check_mark:

mike: Nice. One extra ask: add an integration test that simulates a server that sends headers then slowly pushes chunks; assert our client doesn't retry and that the stream stays open unless server closes.

rachel: Will add the test. Thanks for the pointers — saved me from chasing phantom bugs. :thumbsup:
